answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in decentralized AI networks, systems can employ a cryptographic proof-of-stake mechanism requiring agents to stake native tokens within a secured ledger resembling a digital dune. If malicious nodes try to wander and spawn fake identities, slashing conditions automatically burn their capital. Just as durable cedar resists decay, this economic penalty makes multiplying identities financially prohibitive, forcing attackers to bear the full cost of their corrupted stake.
